nodes.title: Wasmtime M0 escape rate re-derived: 12 escapes reproduce, but the rate swings 0.36-2.2/yr with the denominator; post-1.0 1.2-1.5/yr, critical/high-only 0.5-0.9/yr; aarch64 adds a 2026 critical
nodes.summary: Recomputed from state/raw/round-002/07-data/classified.json (81 unique GHSAs, 2021-05-21..2026-10-19; repo count re-checked by gh api 2026-10-25 = 81, so no new advisories). M0 ESC hits = 14, of which 2 are embedder-only (GHSA-v4cp 2021, GHSA-hgjw 2026), leaving the r3 count of 12. One of those 12 is knob-only (GHSA-44mr zero-pages, 2022), so 11 without it. Denominator: r3 used 5.8 y. The real span 2021-05-21..2026-10-25 is 5.43 y, giving 12/5.43 = 2.21/yr (exact Poisson 95% 1.14-3.86). Since Wasmtime 1.0 (2022-09-20, 4.10 y): 6 escapes (5 without the knob) = 1.22-1.46/yr. Critical/high only: 5 in 5.43 y = 0.92/yr; since 1.0 only ff4p and 897f = 0.49/yr. 3 of the 12 are rated low (xm67, ch89, gw5p). 2024-26: 1 in 2.8 y = 0.36/yr. Underclaim: M0 is defined as x86_64 only. On aarch64 (common on cheap ARM VPS) add GHSA-7f6x (2022) and GHSA-mghf-wjfp-p5xm (critical, 2026-10-19, br_table mis-jump), so 2026 has 2 critical M0-class escapes on aarch64 vs 1 on x86_64.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Hand tags inherited from r2. Per-year n is tiny. The 2026 audit sprint makes the rate non-stationary.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Excluding aarch64 hides a 2026 critical. Excluding 'low' sev items that are still memory-unsafe guest reads/writes understates exposure.
nodes.decision_change: R-ISO-1 direction unchanged. Its reversal trigger (an M0 escape within 6 months) fires with P = 1-exp(-rate*0.5) = 0.16 / 0.45-0.52 / 0.67 at 0.36 / 1.2-1.46 / 2.21 per yr, so at the post-1.0 base rate it is a coin flip and carries no new information. Replace it with '>=3 M0-class escapes in any 12 months' (P about 0.14 at 1.3/yr) or pre-commit P2 to per-tenant processes. R-ISO-2 should name the arch: an aarch64 golden needs >=48.0.7/49.0.4/50.0.0 for GHSA-mghf. GHSA-mghf range: <36.0.19, 37.0.0-<48.0.7, 49.0.0-<49.0.4.

nodes.title: R-PQC-2 FIPS pin aws-lc-fips-sys =0.13.11 carries two open RustSec advisories (CVE-2026-3337, CVE-2026-4428); the FIPS lock fails cargo-audit unless they are ignored with a reachability argument; the aws-lc-rs range is 1.15.1-1.17.2
nodes.summary: OSV query for aws-lc-fips-sys@0.13.11 returns RUSTSEC-2026-0043 / GHSA-65p9-r9h6-22vj / CVE-2026-3337 (AES-CCM tag-verification timing side channel, fixed 0.13.12) and RUSTSEC-2026-0042 / GHSA-9f94-5g5w-gf6r / CVE-2026-4428 (CRL Distribution Point scope-check logic error, fixed 0.13.13). Both are dated March 2026, after 0.13.11 (2026-01-14). Reachability: rustls 0.23.46 aws-lc-rs provider suites are only AES-GCM and ChaCha20-Poly1305 (TLS 1.3 and 1.2), with no CCM, and rustls verifies CRLs in rustls-webpki rather than AWS-LC X.509. So both are likely unreachable through rustls, but reachable if any code calls aws-lc-rs CCM or AWS-LC X.509 directly. crates.io dependency API: aws-lc-rs 1.15.1-1.17.2 all require aws-lc-fips-sys ^0.13.1 (1.15.1 is also compatible; the r3 lower bound of 1.15.2 is unexplained); 1.17.3 ^0.13.16; 1.17.4 ^0.13.17; 1.18.x ^0.14. CMVP MIP 2026-10-25: AWS-LC 4 still 'Comment Resolution - Lab (10/22/2026)', AWS-LC 5 'Pending Review (10/5/2026)'.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Reachability is argued from rustls source, not proved.
nodes.decision_change: R-PQC-2 gate: the FIPS lock's cargo-audit runs with an explicit ignore for RUSTSEC-2026-0042/0043, each with a written reachability argument, plus a CI grep/deny that no workspace crate calls aws_lc_rs CCM or AWS-LC X.509/CRL APIs. Otherwise 'any lock drift off 0.13.11 fails CI' and 'cargo-audit 0 vulns' conflict.

nodes.title: New near-miss in the RLS family: PG master self-join elimination merged RTEs with different securityQuals (RLS qual loss), fixed before release
nodes.summary: postgres/postgres dca6a9e32 (2026-09-29, rowsecurity.sql tests added) fixes a regression from 2ebf25e7d (2026-08-28, 'Perform join removal by editing the query's jointree'). Self-join elimination could merge two RTEs on the same table with different securityQuals 'thereby possibly losing quals that need to be enforced'. The fix restricts SJE to RTEs with equal checkAsUser. 2ebf25e7d is not in REL_19_STABLE (compare: diverged 632/785), so it was master-only (PG 20 dev) and has no CVE. REL_19_STABLE still received 3 SJE fixes on 2026-10-14/15 (86ce68d9e, cbcccca71, 0c45929db). It shows that optimizer rewrites, not only plan caching, can silently drop RLS predicates.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Never shipped in a release, so it does not count toward pred-pg-rls-cve.
nodes.underclaim_risk: PG 19 SJE code is new and churning (3 fixes in Oct).
nodes.decision_change: R-DB-1/R-DB-7: the oracle and the RLS regression gate add self-join / same-table-twice queries under different roles, re-run on every PG minor.

protocol_implications: Commit relabel tables beside recompute scripts; a number that needs hand edits after the script is not reproducible (threat-ledger 61% vs script 60%/46%).

Advisory gates must union OSV/RustSec with repo-level GHSAs (gh api repos/<r>/security-advisories). 7/133 sampled repo advisories, including a cedar HIGH and a 4-month-old cedar LOW, were invisible to OSV on 2026-10-25.
Certified-module pins (FIPS) must carry an explicit advisory-ignore list with reachability arguments; otherwise the 'audit clean' and 'lock frozen to certified source' gates contradict each other.
Reversal triggers must be calibrated against the base rate: a trigger that fires with P~0.5 under the status quo (an M0 escape within 6 months) is not a signal.
Report acceptance tables per scenario; never label a mixed-scenario result as '10 seeds x 10 scenarios'.
Prediction ledger: re-score every round; at-risk items (Kani, sqlx) show that maintainer release cadence must enter p, not just merge status.
